extractor: read directly from the official IRCC pages listed in source_roles
policy: Every entry quotes the official page it was read from. source_excerpt is verbatim government wording, lowercased by the normalizer. Nothing here is paraphrased into a requirement, and nothing is included that the page did not state.
not_extracted: Express Entry is not one program. It is an application-management system for three: the Canadian Experience Class, the Federal Skilled Worker Program and the Federal Skilled Trades Program, each with its own criteria. IRCC publishes those criteria as a side-by-side comparison, so each eligibility requirement below quotes all three columns and names the program each rule belongs to in its own text. None carries a machine rule: VisaAI has no fact for which of the three programs an applicant is pursuing, and gating on a guess would silently hide the criteria that actually apply to them.

The Comprehensive Ranking System points formula. Meeting the minimum criteria only puts a candidate in the pool; IRCC selects by score, and the scoring tables are on a separate 'check your score' page that is not a registered source.
The cut-off score for any round of invitations. IRCC publishes those per round on a separate page.

Full eligibility detail for each of the three programs. Each has its own page (canadian experience class, federal skilled worker program, federal skilled trades program) linked from the navigation but not registered as a source. Only the comparison table on works.html was read.

The Federal Skilled Trades Program's full NOC group list beyond the lead-in. IRCC names major groups 72, 73, 82, 83, 92 and 93, minor group 6320 and unit group 62200, with exclusions for sub-major groups 726 and 932; those are recorded in the requirement description rather than turned into rules, because VisaAI has no NOC fact.

Settlement-funds amounts. The get-your-documents-ready page (registered as 'documents') lists 'proof of funds' but publishes no threshold; the amounts, and which programs are exempt, live on its proof-of-funds sub-page, which is not a registered source.

Language test, education assessment, job offer and police certificate specifics (approved tests, minimum scores, designated assessment organizations, which countries' certificates are needed). The get-your-documents-ready page names each document; the detail is on its sub-pages, which are not registered sources.
Provincial Nominee Program eligibility. IRCC states a nomination gives extra points, but PNP criteria are set by each province and published elsewhere.

Fees as shown on the Express Entry landing page. Its fee widget failed server-side at read time — it renders 'your application: [error loading fee. check the fee list .]' — so all amounts below come from the fee list instead.

A biometrics fee for Express Entry. The landing page states biometrics are part of the after-you-apply stage, but the fee list's biometrics section qualifies the requirement as applying when you apply for 'a visitor visa, study permit or work permit'. That sentence does not cover a permanent residence application, so no biometrics fee is claimed here.
Processing times. The landing page says only 'varies by program'.

The get-your-documents-ready page frames its list as documents 'you may need information from ... when you create a profile'. It does not say which documents IRCC later asks to be uploaded after an invitation to apply; nothing here claims that.

The Venezuelan-passport validity rules on the get-your-documents-ready page (passports issued before June 7, 2019 extended 5 years, with a letter of explanation). VisaAI has no fact for passport issuing country and issue date together, and a rule would have to guess; the passport row's description points to the page instead.

Which programs each document applies to beyond what the page says in its own wording. Only the education item names a program (Federal Skilled Workers); the job offer, trade certificate and provincial nomination items say '(if you have one)' or '(if you applied for the Provincial Nominee Program)', so those four are optional here and carry no rule (VisaAI has no fact for program, job offer, trade certificate or nomination). The other five carry no qualifier on the page and are recorded as required.

requirements.label: You must qualify for one of the three programs Express Entry manages
requirements.description: Canadian Experience Class — for skilled workers with eligible Canadian work experience. Federal Skilled Worker Program — for skilled workers with eligible foreign or Canadian work experience. Federal Skilled Trades Program — for skilled workers qualified in a skilled trade.
requirements.source_excerpt: express entry is an online system that we use to manage immigration applications for 3 programs: canadian experience class for skilled workers with eligible canadian work experience federal skilled worker program for skilled workers with eligible foreign or canadian work experience federal skilled trades program for skilled workers who are qualified in a skilled trade

requirements.label: Meet the language ability threshold for your program
requirements.description: Measured on the Canadian Language Benchmark (CLB), the Canadian standard for measuring an immigrant's English language ability. Canadian Experience Class: CLB 7 for TEER 0 or TEER 1 occupations, CLB 5 for TEER 2 or TEER 3. Federal Skilled Worker Program: CLB 7. Federal Skilled Trades Program: CLB 5 for speaking and listening, CLB 4 for reading and writing.
requirements.source_excerpt: language skills canadian experience class clb 7 for teer 0 or teer 1 occupations clb 5 for teer 2 or teer 3 occupations federal skilled worker program clb 7 federal skilled trades program clb 5 for speaking and listening clb 4 for reading and writing
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Language skills Canadian Experience Class CLB 7 for TEER 0 or TEER 1 occupations CLB 5 for TEER 2 or TEER 3 occupations Federal Skilled Worker Program CLB 7 Federal Skilled Trades Program CLB 5 for speaking and listening CLB 4 for reading and writing

requirements.label: Hold the type of work experience your program requires
requirements.description: Occupations are classified by the National Occupational Classification (NOC), whose six TEER categories are based on the education and training an occupation needs. Canadian Experience Class: Canadian work experience in an occupation in TEER 0, 1, 2 or 3. Federal Skilled Worker Program: work experience in an occupation in one of TEER 0, 1, 2 or 3. Federal Skilled Trades Program: work experience in a skilled trade under key groups of TEER 2 or 3 — major group 72 (technical trades and transportation officers and controllers, excluding sub-major group 726), major group 73 (general trades), major group 82, major group 83, major group 92, major group 93 (excluding sub-major group 932), minor group 6320 (cooks, butchers and bakers) and unit group 62200 (chefs).

requirements.label: Hold the amount of work experience your program requires
requirements.description: Canadian Experience Class: 1 year in Canada in the last 3 years, in any combination of full-time or part-time work. Federal Skilled Worker Program: 1 year continuous within the last 10 years, which may combine part-time, full-time or more than one job in your primary occupation. Federal Skilled Trades Program: 2 years within the last 5 years, in any combination of full-time or part-time work.
requirements.source_excerpt: amount of work experience canadian experience class 1 year in canada in the last 3 years (either combination of full-time or part-time work) federal skilled worker program 1 year continuous within the last 10 years (combination of part-time, full-time or more than 1 job in your primary occupation ) federal skilled trades program 2 years within the last 5 years (either combination of full-time or part-time work)

requirements.label: Job offer — required only for the Federal Skilled Trades Program
requirements.description: Canadian Experience Class: not required. Federal Skilled Worker Program: not required, but a valid job offer earns selection criteria points. Federal Skilled Trades Program: required — either a valid job offer of full-time employment for a total period of at least 1 year, or a certificate of qualification in the skilled trade issued by a Canadian provincial, territorial or federal authority.
requirements.source_excerpt: job offer canadian experience class not required. federal skilled worker program not required, but you can get selection criteria points for having a valid job offer. federal skilled trades program required: a valid job offer of full-time employment for a total period of at least 1 year, or a certificate of qualification in the above skilled trade issued by a canadian provincial, territorial or federal authority
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Job offer Canadian Experience Class Not required. Federal Skilled Worker Program Not required, but you can get selection criteria points for having a valid job offer. Federal Skilled Trades Program Required: a valid job offer of full-time employment for a total period of at least 1 year, or a certificate of qualification in the above skilled trade issued by a Canadian provincial, territorial or federal authority

requirements.label: Education — required only for the Federal Skilled Worker Program
requirements.description: Canadian Experience Class: not required. Federal Skilled Worker Program: secondary education required, with more selection criteria points available for post-secondary education. Federal Skilled Trades Program: not required.

requirements.source_excerpt_display: Education Canadian Experience Class Not required. Federal Skilled Worker Program Secondary education required. You can get more selection criteria points for your post-secondary education. Federal Skilled Trades Program Not required.

requirements.label: Answer the eligibility questionnaire
requirements.description: IRCC offers two routes: the Come to Canada tool, which ends in a personal reference code used to move your information into your Express Entry profile, or the questionnaire inside your IRCC secure account.
requirements.source_excerpt: answer a questionnaire to check if you’re eligible for the minimum requirements of express entry. to answer the questionnaire, you have 2 options: option 1: come to canada tool answer a few questions using the come to canada tool to assess your eligibility. the tool gives you a number at the end (a personal reference code).
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Answer a questionnaire to check if you’re eligible for the minimum requirements of Express Entry. To answer the questionnaire, you have 2 options: Option 1: Come to Canada tool Answer a few questions using the Come to Canada tool to assess your eligibility. The tool gives you a number at the end (a personal reference code).

requirements.label: Create a profile and enter the pool
requirements.description: IRCC invites the candidates with the most points in rounds; only an invited candidate fills out the application.
requirements.source_excerpt: how the express entry process works: create a profile and enter the pool. we'll invite the candidates with the most points in rounds. if you're invited to apply, fill out the application. we'll review your application and make a decision.

requirements.label: Right of permanent residence fee
requirements.description: CAD 600.00. It is already inside the CAD 1,590.00 amounts above — the CAD 990.00 variants are those amounts with this fee removed. IRCC states it is payable before you become a permanent resident, that paying it with the application fees avoids delays, that it is refunded if you withdraw or IRCC refuses the application, and that it does not apply to the dependent children of a principal applicant.
requirements.source_excerpt: right of permanent residence fee fees $can right of permanent residence fee 600.00 for most permanent residence applications, you need to pay the right of permanent residence fee (rprf) when your application is approved. you will have to pay it before you can become a permanent resident.

requirements.label: Consider applying through the Provincial Nominee Program
requirements.description: IRCC presents this as an option, not a requirement: a candidate eligible for one of the three Express Entry programs may also apply through Express Entry for the Provincial Nominee Program, and a nomination earns extra points. PNP criteria are set by each province and were not read. A route to consider, not a document: the nomination itself is the upload slot provincial_nomination.
requirements.source_excerpt: if you’re eligible for one of these programs, you can also apply through express entry for the provincial nominee program. if you’re nominated, you’ll get extra points so you can be invited to apply quickly.
